entries.title: Lottie Web: bounded status motion and lifecycle cleanup
entries.summary: Browser vector-animation integration reference: create one local-data player per surface, stop decorative loops, and destroy the instance when its container is removed.
entries.guidance: Original integration guidance: Use small, meaningful confirmation or progress accents rather than motion as the only status signal. Supply your own licensed local animation JSON; this archive contains code reference text, not playable Lottie data. Honor live prefers-reduced-motion changes by pausing and showing a useful still frame. Avoid perpetual decorative loops, pause offscreen players, and destroy instances on teardown. Renderer choice affects browser cost and fidelity; profile complex masks and oversized compositions.

entries.title: dotLottie Web: canvas playback with deliberate runtime ownership
entries.summary: Canvas Lottie/dotLottie integration guidance grounded in the React adapter's instance reuse and deferred cleanup, without bundling runtime binaries or animation payloads.
entries.guidance: Original integration guidance: Choose canvas playback for compact vector feedback when its renderer tradeoffs fit your browser targets. Bring separately licensed local animation data and a reviewed locally installed runtime; no .lottie, .wasm, native library, or playable animation is archived here. Disable autoplay and looping for reduced motion, retain an informative still state, and update playback when that preference changes. Destroy manually created players on teardown. The React adapter handles its own lifecycle and StrictMode reuse: do not blindly destroy its managed instance from another cleanup. Profile concurrent canvases and pause invisible motion.

entries.title: Reanimated: preference-aware native timing transitions
entries.summary: Native mobile transition guidance from withTiming's configuration and system reduced-motion support, with explicit React Native New Architecture compatibility boundaries.
entries.guidance: Original integration guidance: Use short timing transitions to connect a gesture or explicit state change to its visual result. The pinned README states Reanimated 4.x requires React Native's New Architecture and supported recent React Native versions; verify the exact compatibility matrix before adopting it. Pass ReduceMotion.System instead of overriding the user's accessibility preference. Keep persistent labels and a non-motion indication of state. Prefer transform/opacity work over expensive layout churn, avoid per-frame JS communication, and measure on a real low-end device. No native dependencies or worklet compiler output are included.

entries.title: React Three Fiber: delta-based render-loop motion
entries.summary: React browser 3D motion reference using useFrame subscription, elapsed-frame delta, and static demand rendering for reduced motion.
entries.guidance: Original integration guidance: Reserve a 3D scene for spatial explanation, product inspection, or an intentional interactive accent rather than making every interface animate. useFrame subscribes a mutable callback to the renderer: mutate object refs, use frame delta, and avoid setState or fresh allocations each frame. Stop motion when reduced motion is requested and use demand rendering for a static scene; other interactive changes must invalidate that scene. Pause or unmount hidden canvases, cap device pixel ratio and scene complexity, and provide a meaningful HTML alternative to visual-only canvas content. Scope here is React in a browser, not a claim of universal renderer support.

entries.title: Drei Float: restrained 3D ambient movement
entries.summary: Optional product-scene floating motion based on Float's enabled/speed guard, frame-driven transforms, and demand-render invalidation.
entries.guidance: Original integration guidance: Use a gentle Float treatment only where a 3D object's motion reinforces an intentionally spatial presentation. The inspected component skips updates when disabled or speed is zero and can invalidate a demand-rendered scene while active. Feed it a reactive reduced-motion preference and disable float entirely for that preference. Keep camera and text stable, do not encode essential state through bobbing alone, and avoid stacking multiple looping effects. Budget GPU work and stop hidden scenes. This curated example is for browser React Three Fiber; native exports have different helpers and are not represented by this entry.

entries.title: Rive React: local interactive canvas with managed cleanup
entries.summary: React Rive integration reference grounded in useRive's canvas lifecycle and instance cleanup, not a bundled Rive animation or runtime.
entries.guidance: Original integration guidance: Use a Rive state machine for intentionally interactive visual feedback that would otherwise require many disconnected transitions. Bring your own licensed animation buffer; neither .riv files nor WebAssembly are archived. The hook creates the instance after the canvas exists and owns replacement/cleanup; avoid separately cleaning up its managed instance. Disable autoplay and pause when reduced motion changes, with a useful static alternative. Stop offscreen playback and profile canvas/runtime memory before adding many instances. Give adjacent accessible controls and text the actual interaction semantics; a canvas alone is not a sufficient accessible interface.

entries.title: Rive Flutter: explicit pause/play and loader disposal
entries.summary: Flutter animation lifecycle reference from the pause/play example: bind controller activation to deliberate playback intent and dispose the owned FileLoader.
entries.guidance: Original integration guidance: Use controllable Rive playback for Flutter illustrations and state-machine feedback, while keeping semantic controls and meaningful status text outside the animation. The inspected example uses FileLoader.fromAsset, RiveWidgetBuilder, controller.active, and loader disposal; it references an upstream .riv that is deliberately not downloaded. Supply your own licensed bundled animation and reviewed runtime. Derive playback from explicit user intent and MediaQuery.disableAnimations; reapply it when settings change and pause invisible routes. Dispose the owned loader and follow the exact pinned runtime's ownership rules for controllers. Measure renderer memory and frame cost on target devices; Flutter framework scope is not a promise that every runtime renderer feature works on every deployment platform.

entries.title: VueUse Motion: reactive reduced-motion-aware entrances
entries.summary: Vue browser motion reference combining directive variants with the library's reactive prefers-reduced-motion helper.
entries.guidance: Original integration guidance: Apply one short entrance to establish a newly appearing panel, not to replay every item during ordinary scrolling or reactive updates. The inspected useReducedMotion helper delegates to a reactive media query, so bind variants to its value and do not hide content when reduced motion is requested. Keep transform and opacity changes restrained; avoid layout-heavy animation and offscreen perpetual work. Preserve reading order, focus, and status text. Register MotionPlugin in the host application and verify SSR/hydration behavior separately; this archive is a browser Vue reference, not a mobile runtime or ready-made animation asset.
